title: Get started with kggplot
text: arguments column names. Axis legend titles default variable names, plot type guessed data (scatter plot x y numeric). Everything single call handles:
code: kggplot(   iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species",   title = "Iris", theme = "bw" )

title: Get started with kggplot
text: Give several columns y ("" every column x): kggplot stacks long format colours series. pseudo-column ".series" can mapped aesthetic used facet.
code: kggplot(   iris, "Sepal.Length", c("Sepal.Width", "Petal.Width"),   type = "point", title = "Two variables, one call" ) kggplot(   iris, "Sepal.Length", c("Sepal.Width", "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),   type = "smooth", facet = ".series", facet_args = list(scales = "free_y"),   legend = "none" )

title: Get started with kggplot
text: as_kdata() converts input data frame, time series, matrices plain vectors can plotted directly:
code: kggplot(AirPassengers, title = "Air passengers", theme = "minimal") kggplot(rnorm(200), type = "density", fill = I("grey70"))

title: Get started with kggplot
text: type omitted guessed: line dates time series, points numeric x y, bars categorical x, histogram counts lone x. kgg_types() lists available types.
code: kgg_types() #>  [1] "point"      "jitter"     "line"       "path"       "step"       #>  [6] "area"       "smooth"     "text"       "bar"        "col"        #> [11] "bar_dodge"  "count"      "histogram"  "density"    "ecdf"       #> [16] "cumFreq"    "boxplot"    "violin"     "ribbon"     "pointrange" #> [21] "errorbar"   "hline"      "vline"      "blank"      "convexhull" kggplot(   mtcars, "cyl", fill = "gear", type = "count", palette = "okabe_ito",   title = "Cars by cylinders and gears" ) #> Warning: The following aesthetics were dropped during statistical transformation: fill. #> ℹ This can happen when ggplot fails to infer the correct grouping structure in #>   the data. #> ℹ Did you forget to specify a `group` aesthetic or to convert a numerical #>   variable into a factor?

title: Get started with kggplot
text: character value column, given color, fill group, creates legend entry (color = "Observed"). Use ("red") fixed colour.
code: kggplot(   iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species",   title = "Iris", subtitle = "Sepals", caption = "Source: datasets::iris",   xlab = "Length (cm)", ylab = "Width (cm)", labels = list(color = "Species"),   legend = "bottom", facet = "Species", theme = "bw", base_size = 11 )

title: Get started with kggplot
text: theme bundles ggplot2 theme colour palette one name. kgg_themes() kgg_palettes() list registered ones; theme_<name>() function search path also works (theme = "light").  built-"inrae" theme uses colours INRAE graphic charter. charter sets Raleway titles Avenir Next Pro Condensed text; fonts must installed, kggplot forces none. Opt : Set options(kggplot.theme = "inrae") make theme default session.
code: kggplot(   iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species", facet = "Species",   theme = "inrae" ) options(   kggplot.title_family = "Raleway",   kggplot.base_family = "Avenir Next Condensed" )

title: Get started with kggplot
text: kggplot specification, plots can combined. Layers share one palette one legend, level keeps colour whatever layer comes .  kggplot(p, sim, ...) kgg_add(p, sim, ...) + inherit mappings first layer columns exist new data. Without new data, kgg_add() reuses first layer’s data, handy adding smoother:  ggplot2 component can added +; applied last:  Pipe-friendly modifiers change one thing time leave original untouched:
code: obs <- data.frame(t = 1:10, v = cumsum(rep(1, 10))) sim <- data.frame(t = 1:10, v = cumsum(rep(1.2, 10)))  kggplot(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point", theme = "inrae") +   kggplot(sim, "t", "v", color = "Simulated", type = "line") kggplot(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species") |>   kgg_add(type = "smooth") kggplot(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", theme = "minimal") +   ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed") +   ggplot2::scale_x_log10() p <- kggplot(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species")  p |>   kgg_labs(title = "New title", x = "Sepal length") |>   kgg_theme("bw", base_size = 14) |>   kgg_facet("Species", scales = "free") |>   kgg_legend("bottom")

what: Bands, error bars, reference lines and panel limits
title: Get started with kggplot
text: Four building blocks make multi-panel scientific figure possible kggplot() + : ribbon draws band ymin ymax columns, filled series colour (alpha = 0.2, outline). several y columns, ymin ymax take one column per y, order (single column, shared every series). pointrange errorbar draw point range, black coloured series (map color override). kgg_hline() kgg_vline() add reference lines. Give positions vector draw every panel, data frame holding facet column draw matching panels . Fixed appearance goes arguments: linetype = "dashed", color = ("grey40"). kgg_limits() forces range axes panels, matters free scales: draws nothing trains scales. Layers data share panels facet variable, order, series keeps colour across layers.  formula panel ~ . gives column panels; switch = "y" moves strips left places outside axes. NA removes title: axis titles legend title.
code: dates <- seq(as.Date("2024-05-01"), by = "day", length.out = 60) panels <- c("LAI", "Available water ratio", "Irrigation") simulate <- function(simulation, shift) {   lai <- pmax(0, 3 * sin(seq(0, pi, length.out = 60)) + shift)   awr <- pmin(1, pmax(0, 0.8 - seq(0, 0.5, length.out = 60) + shift / 10))   irr <- ifelse(seq_along(dates) %% 10 == 0, 20 + 5 * shift, 0)   data.frame(     date = rep(dates, 3), simulation = simulation,     panel = factor(rep(panels, each = 60), levels = panels),     mean = c(lai, awr, irr), sd = c(rep(0.3, 60), rep(0.08, 60), rep(0, 60))   ) } sims <- rbind(simulate("Simulation", 0), simulate("Reference", 0.4)) sims$lo <- sims$mean - sims$sd sims$hi <- sims$mean + sims$sd curves <- sims[sims$panel != "Irrigation", ] irrigation <- sims[sims$panel == "Irrigation" & sims$mean > 0, ]  obs <- data.frame(   date = dates[c(10, 25, 40, 55)], lai = c(0.8, 2.4, 2.6, 1.1),   panel = factor("LAI", levels = panels) ) obs$lo <- obs$lai - 0.25 obs$hi <- obs$lai + 0.25 threshold <- data.frame(   panel = factor("Available water ratio", levels = panels), y = 0.4 ) colors <- c(Simulation = "#00a3a6", Reference = "#e07a5f")  kggplot(   curves, "date", "mean", ymin = "lo", ymax = "hi", fill = "simulation",   type = "ribbon", palette = colors, theme = "inrae", legend = "bottom",   facet = panel ~ ., facet_args = list(scales = "free_y", switch = "y"),   xlab = NA, ylab = NA, labels = list(color = NA, fill = NA) ) +   kggplot(curves, "date", "mean", color = "simulation", type = "line",           linewidth = 0.8) +   kggplot(irrigation, "date", "mean", fill = "simulation", type = "bar_dodge",           width = 0.9, position = "dodge") +   kggplot(obs, "date", "lai", ymin = "lo", ymax = "hi", type = "pointrange") +   kgg_hline(data = threshold, yintercept = "y", linetype = "dashed",             color = I("grey40")) +   kgg_vline(dates[c(15, 30, 45)], linetype = "dotted", color = I("grey60")) +   kgg_limits(panel = "Available water ratio", y = c(0, 1))

title: Get started with kggplot
text: as_ggplot() renders specification regular ggplot object, anything easier plain ggplot2. kgg_save() ggplot2::autoplot() also accept kggplot.

title: Get started with kggplot
text: Everything S3 registry: New input class: define as_kdata() method returning data frame. New plot type: kgg_register_type() maps name geom function. New theme palette: kgg_register_theme() kgg_register_palette().
code: kgg_register_palette("traffic", c("#2ecc71", "#f1c40f", "#e74c3c")) kgg_register_theme("traffic", ggplot2::theme_bw, palette = "traffic") kgg_register_type("hollow", ggplot2::geom_point, params = list(shape = 1))  kggplot(   iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species",   type = "hollow", theme = "traffic" )

title: Reference lines and panel limits — kgg_reference
text: kgg_hline() kgg_vline() draw horizontal vertical reference lines. Give positions vector (lines appear every panel), data frame name column holding positions: data frame also facet column, lines appear matching panels (threshold shown one panel ). kgg_limits() forces range axes panels, useful free scales (facet_args = list(scales = "free_y")): draws nothing trains scales, like ggplot2::geom_blank(). Fixed appearance goes arguments: linetype = "dashed", color = ("grey40"), linewidth = 0.5... (wrap colour (), every kggplot layer: bare string legend entry).

title: Reference lines and panel limits — kgg_reference
code: d <- data.frame(   date = rep(as.Date("2024-05-01") + 0:29, 2),   panel = rep(c("Ratio", "Biomass"), each = 30),   value = c(seq(0.2, 0.6, length.out = 30), seq(0, 8, length.out = 30)) ) kggplot(d, "date", "value", type = "line", facet = "panel",         facet_args = list(scales = "free_y")) +   # a threshold in the "Ratio" panel only   kgg_hline(data = data.frame(panel = "Ratio", y = 0.4), yintercept = "y",             linetype = "dashed", color = I("grey40")) +   # decision dates in every panel   kgg_vline(as.Date("2024-05-10") + c(0, 10), linetype = "dotted") +   # the "Ratio" panel spans 0 to 1   kgg_limits(panel = "Ratio", y = c(0, 1))

title: Draw a complete plot in one call — kggplot
code: # scatter plot, coloured, themed: one call kggplot(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species",         title = "Iris", theme = "inrae")   # several y columns at once, long-format handled for you kggplot(iris, "Sepal.Length", c("Sepal.Width", "Petal.Width"),         type = "line")   # univariate types kggplot(iris, y = "Sepal.Length", color = "Species", type = "density")   # time series input kggplot(AirPassengers, title = "Air passengers", theme = "minimal")   # a band around a line, from ymin / ymax columns d <- data.frame(t = 1:20, m = sin(1:20 / 3)) d$lo <- d$m - 0.2 d$hi <- d$m + 0.2 kggplot(d, "t", "m", ymin = "lo", ymax = "hi", type = "ribbon") +   kggplot(d, "t", "m", type = "line")   # superpose a second dataset: consistent colours and a shared legend obs <- data.frame(t = 1:10, v = cumsum(rep(1, 10))) sim <- data.frame(t = 1:10, v = cumsum(rep(1.2, 10))) kggplot(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point", theme = "bw") +   kggplot(sim, "t", "v", color = "Simulated", type = "line")

title: kggplot (development version)
text: New plot types: ribbon (band ymin ymax), pointrange errorbar (black, coloured series), hline vline (reference lines) blank (trains scales). ymin, ymax, xintercept yintercept new aesthetics; several y columns, ymin ymax stacked (one column per y, one shared column). New helpers kgg_hline(), kgg_vline() kgg_limits(): reference lines every panel panels data frame , forced axis limits panels free scales (#7). Layers data now share panels facet variable, order, whatever type (factor character) column. switch facet_args places strips outside axes. kgg_register_type() gains series = "none", free intercept; defaults type (e.g. black colour pointrange) give way aesthetic user maps. Fix: positional aesthetics matched exactly (x longer matches xintercept).

title: kggplot 0.1.0
text: First version, extracted kplot (ggplot2 part) refactored. kggplot() draws complete plot one call: data reshaping (several y columns stacked long format), variables, plot type (guessed omitted), titles, theme, palette, legend facets. result kggplot S3 object, turned ggplot printed (as_ggplot()). Composition: + two kggplot objects (shared colours legend), kggplot(p, data), kgg_add(), ggplot2 components added +. Modifiers: kgg_labs(), kgg_theme(), kgg_palette(), kgg_legend(), kgg_facet(), kgg_save(). as_kdata() (S3) converts input: data.frame, ts, matrix, vector, named list. Extensible registries: kgg_register_type(), kgg_register_theme(), kgg_register_palette(). Built-"inrae" theme palette following INRAE graphic charter v4.2, dependency InraeThemes; fonts can set options(kggplot.base_family = ) options(kggplot.title_family = ). get_color_palette() longer cfg argument: palettes live kggplot registry. “Get started” vignette.
